blocks.etymology: From Middle English thinken, thynken, thenken, thenchen, from Old English þenċan, from Proto-West Germanic *þankijan, from Proto-Germanic *þankijaną (“to think”), from Proto-Indo-European *teng- (“to think, feel, know”). Cognate with Scots think, thynk (“to think”), North Frisian teenk, taanke, tanke, tånke (“to think”), Saterland Frisian toanke (“to think”), West Frisian tinke (“to think”), Dutch denken, dinken (“to think”), Afrikaans dink (“to think”), Low German denken, dinken (“to think”), German denken (“to think”), Danish tænke (“to think”), Swedish tänka (“to think”), Norwegian Bokmål tenke (“to think”), Norwegian Nynorsk tenkja (“to think”), Icelandic þekkja (“to know, recognise, identify, perceive”), Gothic þagkjan (“to think”), Latin tongeō (“know”).

senses.definition: To have a particular opinion, belief, or idea about something.

examples.en: I think that this movie is very interesting.
examples.vi: Tôi nghĩ rằng bộ phim này rất thú vị.

senses.definition: To use your mind to consider something carefully or solve a problem.

examples.vi: Cô ấy đã suy nghĩ cẩn thận trước khi đưa ra lựa chọn cuối cùng.

senses.vi: suy nghĩ; ngẫm nghĩ; nghĩ

senses.definition: To view or consider someone or something in a specific way.
